## November 4: Eilvese reception and a setup notice

**Sources on this page:** p120 A, p120 C. [Concise case study](../radio/nov4_eilvese_and_setup.md).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov4-eilvese-and-setup-november-4-eilvese-reception-and-a-setup-notice"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The embassy reception query contains an ambiguous overprint; its declared frame makes that uncertainty explicit. The separate short setup notice is a native 56-coordinate record. Both preserve all reference and location labels.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov4-eilvese-and-setup-p120-a"></a>

### p120 A

Childs p120, PDF p123; [source crop](../../experiments/nov4_radio_and_departure_queries/sources/p120_A.png). Key: unchanged published **Nov4–6**.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Source transcription — literal received header:**

```text
4th NOVEMBER, 1918.
A) OSM v OUI (11.16 p.m., November 4th)
1950 (4)
RICHI-236
```

**Raw output — conditional 236-slot frame, excluding the overprinted source slot 188; 117/118 fixed positions:**

```text
DEU?SCHMILIATTACHEXXKJDORTX8303X18XISTHELTERTSVERANLASSTXKANN8ORSCHAFTAUCHUNGEDAEMPFTXEILVESEEMPFANGENNACHCHEF4B47883X
```

**Edited output — 7 observed-coordinate substitutions and 1 source-mask fill; same conditional exclusion; 118/118 fixed positions:**

```text
DEUTSCHMILIATTACHEXXZUDORTX8303X18XISTWEITERESVERANLASSTXKANNBOTSCHAFTAUCHUNGEDAEMPFTXEILVESEEMPFANGENNACHCHEF4B47883X
```

</details>

Observed source changes, with zero-based indices: **2 F→V**, **7 V→X**, **34 D→G**, **169 A→V**, **171 G→F**, **186 X→F**, **200 A→V**.

Source-mask fills: **0→A**.

The full edited stream re-encrypts under its stated frame and listed changes.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Deutsch Miliattache. Zu dort 8303.18 ist Weiteres veranlasst. Kann Botschaft auch ungedaempft Eilvese empfangen? Nachchef 4 B 47883.

**Meaning:** The proposed reading addresses the German military attache, refers to 8303.18 and asks whether the embassy can also receive undamped Eilvese transmissions. It does not establish the reception equipment or the outcome of that request.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov4-eilvese-and-setup-six-printed-slots-and-a-conditional-exclusion"></a>

#### Six printed slots and a conditional exclusion

The sixth group of ciphertext row 5 has six spatial glyph positions:
`XXF[T-like overprint]VA`. The literal transcription uses `XXFTVA`, with T
masked as outside the coordinate alphabet. The [detail crop](../../experiments/nov4_radio_and_departure_queries/sources/p120_A_overprint.png)
shows the overstrike. There are **237 source slots**, against `RICHI-236`.
The displayed frame excludes source slot **188**, the masked overprint,
retaining every one of the source's **235 valid coordinates**. A cancellation
is possible, but its intention is not proved; this is a conditional one-slot
exclusion, not a claim of a native five-letter group.

Every local single-slot exclusion is priced against the same proposed text:

| Excluded source slot | Literal | Observed coordinates excluded | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
|185|X|1|6|2|
|186|X|1|6|2|
|187|F|1|7|2|
|188|T-like overprint|0|7|1|
|189|V|1|7|2|
|190|A|1|8|2|

The fewer substitutions in two alternatives are accompanied by deletion of
an observed coordinate and an extra fill. The table is a cost vector, not an
invented single numerical ranking. No other historical damage geometry is
excluded by this local comparison.

The restoration `HELTERTS→WEITERES` is an editorial lexical proposal. It is
not authenticated by a second source. The complete reading preserves the
abbreviations `DEUTSCH MILIATTACHE`, `NACHCHEF` and reference `8303.18`.
The question mark after *empfangen* is editorial question punctuation,
not an extra unresolved decoded position.

### p120 C

Childs p120, PDF p123; [source crop](../../experiments/nov4_radio_and_departure_queries/sources/p120_C.png). Key: unchanged published **Nov4–6**.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Source transcription — literal received header:**

```text
C) UKS v ZON (2.10 a.m., November 5th)
2332 (4)
RIZI-56
```

**Raw output — native 56-slot frame; 28/28 fixed positions:**

```text
0500ABBAUXAPFBAUNAGQBESCEREK
```

**Edited output — 1 observed-coordinate substitution and 0 source-mask fills; 28/28 fixed positions:**

```text
0500ABBAUXAUFBAUNAGQBESCEREK
```

</details>

Observed source changes, with zero-based indices: **51 X→V**.

The full edited stream re-encrypts under its stated frame and listed changes.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> 0500 Abbau. Aufbau NAGQBESCEREK.

**Meaning:** A short notice gives 0500, dismantling and setup, followed by the literal location-like token NAGQBESCEREK. That spelling is not replaced with a modern place-name identity.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov4-eilvese-and-setup-literal-locality-and-time-labels"></a>

#### Literal locality and time labels

The source-visible second group on the last row is `VFVFX`; an early low-resolution transcription of its third glyph as T is rejected by the crop. No historical mask or fill is introduced there. Only `APFBAU→AUFBAU` is proposed. `0500` and `NAGQBESCEREK` stay literal; the latter is not silently changed to a familiar locality spelling.

## p120 / p123 - Three-part instruction to Feigenhaus

**Sources on this page:** p120 B1. [Concise case study](../naval/p120_p123.md).

**Shared edition.** The following reading also discusses [p122 D suffix](122.md#source-p122-d-suffix), [p123 A2](123.md#source-p123-a2), [p123 A3](123.md#source-p123-a3).

<a id="edition-cases-naval-p120-p123-p120--p123---three-part-instruction-to-feigenhaus"></a>


[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Source records](../../experiments/corpus_readings/selected_sources.json) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Records:** p120 B1, the repeated suffix p122 D, and p123 A2-A3.
**Result:** an assembled three-part message under the published Nov4-6 key.
The 461-position reading below is conditional on the repairs in the table:
five valid-coordinate substitutions, nineteen erasure fills and one deletion.
The names and unusual expressions remain literal; their intended referents
have not been established.

**Prior body reading:** George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker
already describe the three-part Feigenhaus/Herkules message in §6.5 of
[*Deciphering ADFGVX messages from the Eastern Front of World War I*](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
printed p24 / author-PDF p25. The present contribution by **icekylinx and
GPT-6 Astra Pro** is the source-level edition, exact repair accounting and
identification of the p122 D repeated suffix. This includes the inherited
prior body of that suffix; it is not a first decipherment of the message.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-p120-p123-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

**Readable German:**

> Feigenhaus, Konstantinopel. Sechshundertsiebzehn. Beichtvater
> zweihundertdreiundneunzig. Nachdem Diktator Anweisung gegeben,
> Notschreie in Andreas nicht vorzunehmen, haben wir uns nochmals mit
> Herkules in Verbindung gesetzt.
>
> Herkules ablehnt Verantwortung fuer neue Notschreie. Infolgedessen
> koennen wir auf keinen Fall neue Notschreie in Andreas vornehmen.
>
> Sie wollen deshalb unseren Anweisungen entsprechend sich verhalten.
> Drahtet, was ihr in Anbetracht veraenderter politischer Lage nunmehr
> zu tun gedenkt. Reichsversorgung.

**Meaning:** The sender reports renewed contact with Herkules after Diktator
instructed that no further *Notschreie* be undertaken in Andreas. Herkules
declines responsibility, so the prohibition stands. The recipient is to follow
these instructions and telegraph the action now intended in view of the
changed political situation. The opening names Feigenhaus in Constantinople
and the references 617 and 293, written out as words in the ciphertext.

*Notschreie* literally means cries for help. Together with Feigenhaus,
Beichtvater, Diktator, Andreas, Herkules and Reichsversorgung, it may belong
to a special vocabulary. This edition does not substitute guessed people,
places, institutions or operations for these terms. The irregular telegram
word order and the shift from *Sie* to *ihr* are retained. Word spacing,
punctuation and capitalization are editorial.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-p120-p123-source-support"></a>

### Source support

| Part | Source slots and raw reading | Exact cost of the displayed candidate |
|---|---|---|
| [p120 B1](../../sources/excerpts/other_p120_B1.png) | 394 slots; all 197 raw positions fixed | One coordinate substitution: raw `ANWEISYNG` becomes `ANWEISUNG`. |
| [p123 A2](../../sources/excerpts/other_p123_A2.png) | 232 slots; 97/116 raw positions fixed | Fill 18 printed dashes and one unreadable glyph; change two valid coordinates. |
| [p123 A3](../../sources/excerpts/other_p123_A3.png) | 297 printed slots against the declared 296 | Delete one of two adjacent `A` coordinates, then make two substitutions for `ANBETRACHT` and `LAGE`. |

The [p122 D intercept](../../sources/excerpts/other_p122_D_suffix.png) is an
**exact 164-coordinate suffix** of p120 B1, starting at zero-based source
index 230. It independently confirms that part of the transmitted stream.
It is not decrypted as a separate short message: changing the transposition
frame to 164 would change the column boundaries.

For part 3, the source visibly prints the eleven-coordinate sequence
`VAAXX VXXAVA`. Deleting source index **211 or 212** gives the same repaired
stream. Among all 297 one-coordinate deletions, these are the only two
minimizers for the **stated candidate**, each requiring two further
valid-coordinate substitutions. This candidate-specific check does not
prove that every possible German reading has been considered.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-p120-p123-assembly-dates-and-credit"></a>

### Assembly, dates and credit

The source labels the parts `1 TL`, `2 TL`, `3 TL` and `3 TEILE`.
The p120 header is `OSM v OUI (8.32 p.m., November 4th); 1956`;
p122 repeats its suffix at 8.33 p.m. with `1056`, and p123 supplies parts 2
and 3 at 8.40 p.m., also with `1056`. The differing four-digit fields are
retained. The route, part labels and exact repeated suffix support the
assembly. No date is changed to fit the period key.

The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, printed pp. 120, 122-123 / PDF pp. 123, 125-126 in the
[public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The complete Nov4-6 key retains its attribution to George Lasry and the
historical/research sources in [the key register](../../data/keys.json).
Source assembly, inspection, repair accounting and this edition:
**icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first historical decipherment priority
is claimed.

```sh
python3 experiments/corpus_readings/verify.py --verify
```

The [certificate](../../experiments/corpus_readings/certificates.json)
preserves the unchanged source, every plaintext-to-coordinate map, the exact
suffix match and all deletion trials. Every complete candidate re-encrypts
to its explicitly repaired source.
